passages.context: The complete English declaration was read: the question whether there has been 'any change in the Church's decision in regard to Masonic associations since the new Code of Canon Law does not mention them expressly, unlike the previous Code'; the editorial-criterion answer ('contained in wider categories'); the operative sentences 'the Church's negative judgment in regard to Masonic association remains unchanged since their principles have always been considered irreconcilable with the doctrine of the Church and therefore membership in them remains forbidden. The faithful who enrol in Masonic associations are in a state of grave sin and may not receive Holy Communion.'; the denial that local ecclesiastical authorities may 'give a judgment on the nature of Masonic associations which would imply a derogation', in line with the declaration of 17 February 1981; John Paul II's approval and publication order; the date; and the signatures of Cardinal Ratzinger and Archbishop Hamer.

work.author: Sacred Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith
work.description: The CDF declaration of 26 November 1983 (AAS 76 [1984] 300), signed by Cardinal Ratzinger and approved and ordered published by John Paul II: occasioned by the new Code's omission of express mention of Masonic associations, it attributes the omission to an editorial criterion, declares the Church's negative judgment unchanged because Masonic principles 'have always been considered irreconcilable with the doctrine of the Church', states that membership remains forbidden and that the faithful who enrol 'are in a state of grave sin and may not receive Holy Communion', and denies local ecclesiastical authorities competence to derogate.
work.title: Declaratio de associationibus massonicis (Quaesitum est, 26 November 1983)
